evidence.quote: You can concatenate together multiple strings to make a single string.

evidence.claim: Parameterized queries separate SQL statements from parameter values.
evidence.quote: The core idea of parameterized queries is to separate SQL statements from parameter values.
evidence.title: Parameterized SQL Queries: An In-Depth Analysis of Security and Performance
sub_questions: How do parameterized queries separate data from code to prevent injection?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states that parameterized queries separate SQL statements from parameter values, matching the claim.

evidence.claim: User input is treated as a plain string value, preventing additional SQL execution.
evidence.quote: Thus, even if user input contains malicious code, the database treats it as a plain string value, preventing additional SQL execution.
evidence.title: Parameterized SQL Queries: An In-Depth Analysis of Security and Performance
sub_questions: How do parameterized queries separate data from code to prevent injection?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states that user input is treated as a plain string value, preventing additional SQL execution.

evidence.claim: Manual escaping is fragile and can fail to prevent injection.
evidence.quote: - Manual escaping is a fragile last resort; reach for it only when no parameterized option exists.
evidence.title: SQL Injection Prevention: Complete Guide with Code Examples…
sub_questions: Why can manual escaping of strings fail to prevent injection?
evidence.support_reason: Quote says manual escaping is fragile, but does not explicitly mention injection failure.

evidence.claim: Manual escaping is fragile and error-prone because different databases and contexts have subtle escaping rules, making it easy to miss edge cases that attackers can exploit.
evidence.quote: Manually escaping special characters (like doubling single quotes) is sometimes suggested as a lighter-weight fix, but it's fragile and error-prone in practice — different databases and contexts have different, subtle escaping rules, and it's easy to miss an edge case (encoding issues, alternate quote characters, database-specific syntax quirks) that a determined attacker can exploit.
evidence.title: SQL Injection: Prevention Guide | sqlint
sub_questions: What common mistakes in manual escaping lead to vulnerabilities?
evidence.support_reason: The quote explicitly states that manual escaping is fragile and error‑prone, cites subtle escaping rules across databases and contexts, and notes that missing edge cases can be exploited by attackers.

evidence.claim: Manual escaping is not equivalent to parameterized queries for security.
evidence.quote: Escaping should never be treated as equivalent to parameterization for security purposes.
evidence.title: SQL Injection: Prevention Guide | sqlint
